summary: Self-Verified Distillation samples n candidate solutions to unlabeled OpenThoughts seed questions, filters them with the same model through a UQ-style prompt cascade (cycle-consistency, factuality, correctness; unanimous votes at strength v), and SFTs on the survivors. Qwen3-0.6B/4B/8B improve on held-out math (AIME26, HMMT), science (GPQA-D, HLE) and code (LiveCodeBench v5/v6) without teachers, tools or ground truth, and mostly beat spending the same verifier at test time.

claims.claim: For Qwen3-4B, aggregate held-out pass@1 improves +16.7 (math), +11.1 (science), +8.3 (coding).
claims.evidence: Table 2 reports Mean Δ +8.4 / +5.6 / +4.2. The abstract figures are sums of two benchmark deltas (10.0+6.7, 9.6+1.5, 3.9+4.4), roughly doubling the apparent effect. §4.2 text cites code +4.2/+6.7, which does not match Table 2 (+3.9/+4.4).

claims.claim: Filtering is necessary; unfiltered self-generated code data hurts.
claims.evidence: Fig. 3: NoFilter below initial model on LCBv5/v6, verified data above.

claims.claim: Multi-stage UQ verifier beats a simple correctness prompt.
claims.evidence: Table 1: Mean Δ +8.4 vs +4.9 on math, Qwen3-4B, one training run each.

claims.claim: Training on verified data beats test-time verification (UQ-TTC) in most settings at 1 vs up to 168 inference calls.
claims.evidence: Table 3: better in 5 of 6 math comparisons; 8B AIME26 UQ-TTC wins 67.7 vs 64.7. Data-construction compute is not reported in comparable units.

patterns.note: Self-training/SFT on self-verified data improves small Qwen3 models; no RL.
Prompt-based self-verification is useful as a data filter (Table 1), but the authors warn it may accept incorrect solutions; precision of the filter is never measured against ground truth.

methodology.sample: Seed questions: 53,125 math, 26,041 science, 9,168 code from OpenThoughts; held-out tests AIME26, HMMT 02/25, GPQA Diamond, HLE, LCBv5, LCBv6.
methodology.baselines: Initial model; NoFilter; simple verifier; UQ-TTC. No comparison with other self-training methods (e.g. STaR-style with answer checking, majority-vote pseudo-labels) or teacher distillation.
methodology.variance: Evaluation averaged over 3-10 sampling seeds per benchmark; a single training run per configuration; no CIs on deltas.
methodology.ablations: n x v grid; verifier type; selection policy (App. C.4); model scale.
methodology.contamination_controls: Uses recent AIME26/HMMT and later LCB windows as held-out tests; no explicit decontamination of OpenThoughts seeds against tests.
methodology.languages: Code tasks are LiveCodeBench (competitive programming, predominantly Python).

standards.artifacts: No code/data URL found; prompts in App. B-C. Part of the Marin Project.

biases.detail: Abstract reports summed two-benchmark deltas as 'aggregate' gains, double the per-benchmark mean in Table 2; title framing 'Secretly Its Own Synthetic Data Pipeline'.
One training run per config; HLE gains of +1.5 on low single-digit base scores are likely within noise.
Training-time generation and verification compute (n=8, v=5 cascade over ~88k seeds) not quantified against the UQ-TTC comparison.
Code gains quoted in §4.2 (+4.2/+6.7) differ from Table 2 (+3.9/+4.4).

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Qwen3 (Alibaba) open models; no author affiliation with Alibaba.
coi.funding: Schmidt Sciences; compute from Google TPU Research Cloud; Marin Project.
coi.detail: Academic; compute grant from Google does not bear on the evaluated product.

verdict_reason: off-topic: LLM post-training on math/science/competitive-programming, not agents or software-engineering harnesses. The study is also weakened by an abstract that doubles reported gains, a single model family and single training runs.
applicability: No direct transfer: a Java backend team adopting agent hosts will not fine-tune models. The only harness-relevant lesson is indirect. A decomposed verifier (back-translate the solution to the question, then check facts, then correctness) beat a single 'is this correct?' prompt. If the team uses an LLM to check generated healthcare education content against its source or spec, a structured multi-check cascade is preferable to one judge prompt, but deterministic checks should still gate.

conflicts_with.detail: That paper (per its abstract) finds self-authored verification unreliable in self-improving agents, with self-scores near perfect while real performance degrades. Here self-verification is reported to improve held-out results, though the filter's precision is never measured.
